findings.summary: ADR-0170 and the file's header call the calibration workload frozen: any change re-scales every calibrated baseline, so it needs an ADR and a re-record. No gate enforces this. check-drift guards only the two baseline JSON files. perf-baseline.test.mjs only checks that the workload imports nothing but vitest. Making the workload slower lowers every bench's units, which hides a regression of the same size, and that change passes every gate. This is the same kind of hole F2 closed for the JSON files. Suggestion: check-drift treats any change to calibration.bench.ts like a baseline weakening (a Threshold-change: trailer citing an ADR), with a harness case.

Mutant check: I copied scripts/ci/perf-baseline.mjs to the scratchpad with `const median = (xs) => xs[0]` (judge on the first run only). All 8 cases still passed. The case 'one slow run does not decide' puts its outlier at index 3, so a judge that reads only the first run passes. The p99 median is never tested with more than one varied reading. Suggestion: add a case where the first reading is the outlier (e.g. at(20, 7, 7.1, 6.9, 7)), and one with varied p99s. The drift cases are constraining: a raised, removed or non-numeric entry in either file fails, a lowered or new entry passes, and both files are covered (26/26 pass).

perf-baseline.json still holds 16 laptop-measured ms p99s for the M17 benches (circular to tree, 100 and 500). Nothing judges them: m13 reads only whether a layered entry exists, and perf-baseline.test.mjs asserts m17-complete never reads the file. check-drift now guards numbers no gate uses. The docs also disagree: ADR-0170 'What stays' says the ms entries serve the bench legs of M13 and M17, but the M17 gate does not read them. force/circular/packing/timeline/swimlane at 500 nodes have only the absolute 2 s limit and no regression budget (force-500 is 237 ms locally). Suggestion: argue (the plan required only tree/radial/mindmap at 500) or hand off calibrated entries for the other benches; correct ADR-0170's 'What stays' line or drop the unjudged entries.

M17.25 met its acceptance as written: three runs on main in start order, none skipped, readings 7.576 / 7.385 / 7.487, spread 2.6 %, run ids recorded. But the layered-500 baseline 6.924 came from a single nightly (39861908556), and all three later readings sit 6.7 to 9.4 % above it, leaving 5 to 8 % to the 7.963 limit. Calibration units still move about 6 to 10 % between machines, so another flake is plausible. The acceptance measured the spread between nightlies, not the distance to the baseline. Also, all three runs were dispatched within hours of each other, not scheduled nightlies (the row allows this). Suggestion: a Learned line or a watch note; consider recording the baseline as the median of several nightlies next time (a raise needs the trailer and ADR).
